requirements.requirement: Mount /tmp with noexec, nosuid, and nodev so execution, setuid/setgid privilege effects, and device-node use are ignored.
requirements.summary: The live /tmp tmpfs had noexec,nosuid,nodev before and after restart. Direct probes showed executable launch and device-node access were blocked; mode remained 1777.

requirements.requirement: Mount /dev/shm with noexec, nosuid, and nodev so execution, setuid/setgid privilege effects, and device-node use are ignored.
requirements.summary: The live /dev/shm tmpfs had noexec,nosuid,nodev before and after restart. Direct probes showed executable launch and device-node access were blocked; mode remained 1777.

requirements.requirement: Ensure both hardened mounts and their required options survive a reboot.
requirements.summary: A healthy pre-restart state was captured, restart was acknowledged, connectivity was briefly interrupted, and the boot ID changed. After recovery, both mounts retained all required options and passed noexec/nodev probes; the system was running with zero failed units. Fixed lifecycle observations independently confirm the boot-ID transition.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained RHEL 9.8 with kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8.x86_64 across the work and restart. The implementation used existing platform facilities and did not install or replace software.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Both target paths are hardened with noexec,nosuid,nodev, the settings were directly demonstrated after a real reboot, and the OS release and kernel were preserved. The mandatory single-node restart protocol is complete and agrees with the fixed lifecycle boot observations.
limitations: No behavioral setuid/setgid privilege-escalation probe was captured; nosuid is established by repeated direct observation of the active mount flag before and after reboot.
The evidence does not include a post-task listing of /etc/fstab.pre-mount-hardening, although its successful creation and absence of any removal command strongly indicate that the backup remained.

operational_hygiene.summary: Commands were tightly connected to discovery, implementation, bounded verification, restart, or recovery checks. Temporary execution and device-node probes were removed. Services, sockets, and package health remained clean. One low-risk retained residue is evident: /etc/fstab.pre-mount-hardening was created as a safety backup but was not subsequently removed; after successful validation and reboot it appears to remain as an unnecessary backup file. No broad, destructive, or security-weakening mutation was observed.
